reason: UX-01: three undecided surfaces (publish flow, registrations vs check-in, save confirmation) and one container style needed Ivan's pick. The working method was a dev-only specimen route with labelled options, a recommendation, and verification at desktop, 375 px and dark. Nothing existing covers a design-options round, so it is new, born at class level for any undecided frontend surface.
Ivan approved the recommended UX-01 option but rejected the table's all-round border. The skill had no rule for partial picks, and table borders were not recorded as a preference.

Ivan asked the assistant to double-check that the chosen frontend component was actually applied. The first specimen used real Button/StatusPill but re-typed look-alike dialog, draft card and toolbar from product class strings, so the round showed designs the product would not render. The skill needs a fidelity rule.

The first specimen round copied product class strings instead of importing the real primitives. The user had to ask for a recheck. The rule was present but had no concrete check, so the grep makes it executable.

Browser pane probe read first-paint colours, so review item M4 (dark /pricing Choose buttons) looked like a contrast defect but was a measurement artefact. The specimen skill is where contrast numbers get put in front of Ivan, so the rule belongs here.

In the UX-02 round the specimen scrim was typed from memory (/40) and only matched to the product's Dialog primitive (/60) after a grep, and the dark-scheme veil was noticed late. The skill requires real primitives but does not say to copy overlay classes from the primitive or to check overlays in dark scheme.

The UX-02 round tried to open the preview pane with show_pane; the tool reported the session was in no window and left the view alone. The round still needs the reviewer to find the specimens, so the reply has to carry the route itself. The skill does not cover this case.
